abstract: Background: Reduction in nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability is postulated to drive the progression of cardiometabolic diseases (CMDs), such as heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. The potent NO scavenger, hemoglobin alpha (Hba), regulates endothelial-derived NO in health and disease. Whether lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) express Hba to modulate NO signaling and promote CMD is unknown. Methods: We generated LEC-specific Hba wildtype and knockout mice and fed them a high fat, high sucrose diet to investigate the role of LEC Hba in CMD progression. To further define the necessity of LEC-derived NO in preventing CMD phenotypes, we generated LEC-specific endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) wildtype and knockout mice and subjected them to normal chow feeding. Results: We found genes encoding Hba were upregulated in the heart during CMD and that Hba was enriched in cardiac lymphatic vessels. Genetic deletion of Hba from LECs prevented CMD-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and reductions in cardiac lymphatic density. Notably, our data demonstrate this occurred independent of changes in the coronary blood vasculature and was driven by local, rather than systemic, changes in NO. Scavenging of NO in vitro increased LEC expression of immunoregulatory genes, aligning with Hba-mediated regulation of immune cell, and more specifically T cell, presence in the heart observed in CMD. Mechanistic studies in vitro revealed modulation of NO around LECs did not impact T cell activation, but instead adhesion ? findings which were validated in vivo. Deletion of eNOS from LECs in otherwise healthy mice recapitulated CMD phenotypes of reduced cardiac lymphatic density, cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, and T cell enrichment in the heart. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate LEC Hba regulates local NO signaling during CMD to promote cardiac hypertrophic remodeling and inflammation. Thus, disruption of Hba function in LECs poses as a potential therapeutic approach in CMDs associated with reduced NO bioavailability.
